s: Brigham Young University-Idaho runs on a three track system including Fall, Winter, and Spring Semesters. Each semester will have the same or similar events and deadlines, but the dates and days will differ per semester and per year. Visit theAcademic Calendar to see all important dates and deadlines for First Blocks, Second Blocks, and Full Semesters.

To take classes, you must apply to the university as a visiting student. See BYU Visiting Students for more information. Semester-length classes are classes that span both spring and summer terms (starting on the first day of spring term and ending on the last day of summer term.)

All students have the same priority registration date for spring and summer: March 1. Your assigned priority registration date is determined by the number of credit hours earned through the most recently completed semester/term.

A revised academic calendar proposal was approved by the Board of Trustees in January 2017 and BYU–Hawaii will be implementing this new calendar for the 2017-18 academic year. The new calendar starts in September and goes through June. It features 15-week fall and winter semesters and a compressed 9-week spring semester in which students will take 8 credits to be full-time.
